title: Natural augmented computation of ordinary quotient reduction
statement: Let l be prime and E a finite extension of Q_l, and W an arbitrary scheme. Fix a coherent derived coefficient-system calculus S of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] and an ordinary reduction A of [def-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model-data], including its natural evaluation isomorphisms to actual scalar extension and every ordinary quotient square. On the full category of flat-term K-flat complexes, there is a natural isomorphism goodLocalization⋙S.reduction ≅ goodInclusion⋙A.functor.mapHomologicalComplex⋙Q. For every good complex P, its component and the termwise A evaluation isomorphisms satisfy CoefficientReductionPresentation and IntegralOpenReduction.AugmentedPresentation. Thus the computation is pinned by the transpose of one entire strict chain scalar-unit augmentation, not by its evaluated arrows alone. No completeness, boundedness or quasi-compactness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YY, 0941 and 09T5: deriving the ordinary quotient/limit adjunction on good models, with strict scalar-unit normalization.

proof.text: Use the ordinary model supplied by fixedCalculusModels. Compare its tensor functor with A using M.evaluation followed by the inverse of A.evaluation at every level. The two quotient equations give the successor squares. The sequenceIsoOfSuccessor construction and sequence_hom_ext assemble these finite isomorphisms into a natural isomorphism of sequence-module functors.

Transport the ordinary tensor/limit adjunction along this natural isomorphism. Naturality of inverse-limit projections and of coefficientSequenceRestriction_evaluation, together with the finite comparison equation, preserves the actual scalar-unit formula. Keep the original termwise-limit comparison and its projection equations.

Apply fixedDerivedComparison to this transported ordinary model, the canonical termwise-limit comparison and the canonical normalized right-derived constant-limit unit. Its comparison is invertible on flat-term K-flat complexes, so restrict it to obtain the required natural isomorphism e. Its finite evaluation equation gives the first presentation condition, and A.quotient gives the second degreewise.

Transpose the transported ordinary unit through the constant-tower/limit adjunction on complexes, inserting the composition comparison between termwise restriction followed by termwise limit and their composite. This constructs a strict chain augmentation a. Its degree-i, level-n component is the ordinary unit followed by the inverse-limit projection. The transported unit formula, the actual scalar-extension unit formula and cancellation of A.evaluation show precisely the required heterogeneous section equality.

For any strict constant-tower chain map, the defining factorization equation of the derived adjunction unit and naturality of the right-derived limit unit identify its derived transpose with the localized ordinary transpose followed by the canonical limit comparison and unit. Apply this to a. The termwise-limit projection equations identify the two comparisons; fixedDerivedComparison gives the same normalized transpose for e. Naturality in the restriction-factor isomorphism completes AugmentedPresentation.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryReductionAugmentedComputation (W : Scheme.{t})
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W)
    (cS : CoefficientDerivedSystemCoherence l E W S) (A : OrdinaryReduction l E W) :
    ∃ e : integralOperationsGoodLocalization l E W ⋙ S.reduction ≅
      (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).ι ⋙
        A.functor.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q,
      ∀ P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E W).FullSubcategory,
        CoefficientReductionPresentation l E W S.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReduction
          P.obj P.property.1 _ (e.app P) (A.complexEvaluation l E P.obj) ∧
        IntegralOpenReduction.AugmentedPresentation l E W S P.obj _ (e.app P)
          (A.complexEvaluation l E P.obj)
